texts.title: Sure you remember it right?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: recall the last appointment you agreed on… which day?
texts.hook.h2.frame: « Sure as I see you »… wrong?
texts.hook.h2: « Sure as I see you »… so could you be wrong?
texts.hook.h3.frame: Sure… but it was Nour's words
texts.hook.h3: I was sure about the date… turns out I remembered Nour's words, not what I heard.
texts.hook.h4: An experiment in 10 countries: did people trust their own eyes… or their colleague's words?
texts.hook.h5.frame: Sure… saw it, or heard it?
texts.hook.h5: The thing you're sure of… did you see it yourself? Or did someone tell you?
texts.s1.n1: This is Karim, out of the boss's meeting.
texts.s1.l2: The boss said delivery is on Sunday.
texts.s1.a4: And you… if someone told you another day?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time Karim writes down what he heard.
texts.s1.l6: The boss said delivery is on Sunday.
texts.s1.l7: I wrote Thursday… shall we ask him?
texts.book.card: Our memories change easily… so hold your certainty more lightly.
texts.book.l1: The book says: we forget and mix things up… so don't cling too tightly to what you remember.
texts.book.l2: Like a moment from your childhood: you heard about it so often… you came to remember it.
texts.verdict.nuance: Your first certainty carries weight, but it's no proof… after talk and time, you can stay sure and be wrong.
texts.verdict.l2: In 10 countries, after a film, many answered with a detail they heard from a colleague… not what they saw.
texts.verdict.l3: And some people, told it often enough, remembered getting lost as children… it never happened.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Karim: write down what was said before any talk… and go back to it when you disagree. It may help.
texts.share: Send this to someone you always argue with about « who said what ».
